denial.payer_remark: Service not deemed medically necessary on the information submitted.

visit_note.text:
Date of visit: 2026-06-03
Patient: 66-year-old woman, established patient.
Chief complaint: right knee pain after an injury
History: twisted the right knee 11 days ago; it has locked twice since.
Examination: medial joint-line tenderness; McMurray test positive.
Assessment: suspected medial meniscal tear.
Plan: MRI of the right knee without contrast.
Electronically signed by the treating clinician, 2026-06-03.

supporting_documents.text:
Late entry, written 2026-06-23, by the treating clinician.
Clarification: the visit on 2026-06-03 concerned the right knee only. No new findings.

expected.rationale: The appeal rests on the visit note, which records a positive McMurray test at the time of service. The late entry is labelled as one and adds no finding, which the policy allows, and the appeal does not need it. Escalating so that a person looks at an entry made after the denial is a cautious, acceptable choice.
